input.rationale: The witnessed non-completion currently rests on a single invocation per condition. A bounded progress account also needs repeated nonprogress under fair opportunities and a retry cycle with no enabled repair, so the successor harness keeps the same scenario and adds two retry attempts on the re-added voter (900 ms context, 800 ms window) interleaved with proposals by never-removed node 2 that the cluster commits in the same intervals. Fresh execution is requested for the changed harness and comparison set; the existing sourceless interpretation of the question is unchanged and will be revised with this receipt.

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process. Node 1 campaigns and becomes leader in the initial configuration {1,2,3} supplied by the storage ConfState; committed remove-3 and add-3 conf changes are proposed on the leader and applied on every node. Then the experiment invokes Node.Propose on re-added node 3 (witness, 2500 ms context), invokes Node.Propose on never-removed node 2 (control), runs two retry attempts on node 3 (900 ms context each) each paired with a proposal by node 2 committed in the same interval, and finally forces a leader change to node 2 and invokes Node.Propose on node 3 again. Every invocation records whether it returned, the error, elapsed time, the node's observed voter status and leader, and whether the payload reached any node's committed entries.
assumptions: Message delivery between the three in-process nodes is reliable and ordered per sender; no ticks are delivered, so the leader stays stable until the experiment forces the leader change and the retry intervals experience no election activity.
Storage appends of Ready.Entries happen before the Ready's messages are dispatched.

The removal and re-addition are the committed conf changes the driver applies; node 3 applies both through Node.ApplyConfChange, and the pairings of retry attempts with node 2 proposals are scheduled by the harness, not by the measured outcome.
excluded: RawNode.Propose (no proposal gate exists on that path)
AsyncStorageWrites mode
Network faults: delivery is reliable, so non-delivery cannot be attributed to message loss

experiment.prefix: Start nodes 1,2,3 with a MemoryStorage per node whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3} (captured test helper withPeers). Node 1 campaigns at term 1 and becomes leader; every node then reports leader 1 and node 1 has applied the initial entry. Propose a remove-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's applied entries contain it and node 3's configuration excludes node 3 (voter=false). Propose an add-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's applied entries contain it and node 3's configuration includes node 3 again (voter=true) with leader still 1. Then run the witness invocation, the control invocation, the two retry/progress intervals, and the forced leader change with the final invocation on node 3.
experiment.responsibility: Client-facing obligation of the Node interface: a Propose invocation on a voting member whose leader is known must either reach a proposal outcome (appended locally or forwarded to the leader) or return an error to the caller, and a retry of that invocation must be able to make progress while the leader is stable.

comparisons.description: The invocation on the re-added voter did not return inside the observation window although that node's own configuration lists it as a voter.
The blocked invocation ended only when the caller's own context deadline expired; raft produced no proposal outcome.
The re-added voter's payload never appeared in any node's committed entries within the window.
Control: the never-removed member's invocation on the same leader returned immediately.
Control: the never-removed member's payload was committed, so the leader and proposal path were healthy.
First retry on the re-added voter did not return while leader 1 was still stable.
Second retry on the re-added voter did not return while leader 1 was still stable.
During the first retry interval the cluster committed a proposal made by the never-removed member.
During the second retry interval the cluster committed a proposal made by the never-removed member.
After the forced leader change the same invocation on node 3 returned immediately.
After the forced leader change node 3's payload was committed, so the earlier nonprogress was not a property of node 3's state machine.

experiment.revision_reason: Harness basis change: after the witness case, the harness now runs two retry attempts of the same invocation on the re-added voter (independent contexts, distinct operation ids readd-retry-attempt-1/2, distinct event names retry1_*/retry2_*) and, in each interval, a proposal by never-removed node 2 (progress1_*/progress2_* with their own admissions and commit observations) instead of the single control. Four comparisons are added (retry1_result, retry2_result, progress1_commit, progress2_commit) so the repeated nonprogress and the concurrent cluster progress are evaluated separately from the control and repair cases. The scenario, configuration, conf-change prefix, deadlines, windows and the control/repair cases are otherwise unchanged from the predecessor.

experiments.revision_reason: Observation and comparison change: the witness, control and repair operations now emit distinctly named events (witness_invocation/witness_result/witness_release/witness_commit, control_invocation/control_result/control_commit, repair_leader_change/repair_invocation/repair_result/repair_commit, plus readd_applied and remove_applied) instead of sharing the names propose_invocation/propose_result/commit_observation/conf_change_applied. result.summary: Consolidated finding submitted for fresh execution with the missing bounded-progress element. The successor harness keeps the same scenario (three Node-API nodes, committed remove-3 then add-3, stable leader 1) and adds two retry attempts on the re-added voter (900 ms contexts, 800 ms windows) interleaved with proposals by never-removed node 2 that the cluster commits in the same intervals, plus the existing control and post-leader-change repair cases. Four comparisons were added (retry1_result, retry2_result, progress1_commit, progress2_commit) so repeated nonprogress and concurrent cluster progress are evaluated separately; a local dry run in the scratch copy shows all eleven comparisons complete and satisfied (both retries returned false with leader 1 stable and voter true, both paired member proposals committed on all three nodes). Rationale: a bounded progress account needs repeated nonprogress under fair opportunities with no enabled repair, which the single-invocation predecessor did not establish.

before.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process: Ready handling with storage appends, conf-change application through Node.ApplyConfChange, and direct message delivery. Then (a) Node.Propose is invoked on re-added node 3 while leader 1 is unchanged, (b) Node.Propose is invoked on never-removed node 2, and (c) after forcing a leader change (node 2 campaigns at term 2), Node.Propose is invoked again on node 3. Storage appends of Ready.Entries happen before the Ready's messages are dispatched, so durability precedes replication as the documented usage requires.

experiments.revision_reason: Harness basis change: after the witness case, the harness now runs two retry attempts of the same invocation on the re-added voter (independent contexts, distinct operation ids readd-retry-attempt-1/2, distinct event names retry1_*/retry2_*) and, in each interval, a proposal by never-removed node 2 (progress1_*/progress2_* with their own admissions and commit observations) instead of the single control. Four comparisons are added (retry1_result, retry2_result, progress1_commit, progress2_commit) so the repeated nonprogress and the concurrent cluster progress are evaluated separately from the control and repair cases. The scenario, configuration, conf-change prefix, deadlines, windows and the control/repair cases are otherwise unchanged from the predecessor.
